newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says privatisation, inflation are priority.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says privatisation, inflation are priority.

text.p: Turkey's new secularist government said in a document to be released on Monday that jump starting stalled privatisations and fighting inflation were its main economic targets.
"Priority will be given to the struggle against inflation," said a government document to be read out in parliament by Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz later in the day.
Inflation has been the bane of Turkish governments for more than a decade. The annual consumer price index stands at 78 percent.

"Our government will carry out reforms that take into account the country's long-term interests and needs and are not just aimed at getting by," said the document, a policy blueprint obtained by Reuters ahead of Yilmaz's address.
Attempts to balance the budget with the help of a wave of privatisations were hindered by fights between the army and the previous government, an Islamist-led coalition that quit last month.
The new administration is a left-right coalition that is expected to pass a confidence vote in parliament on July 12 and take the country to early elections next year.
It says it has inherited a gaping hole in the budget.
"In the first months of the year the budget balance has shown a deficit of hundreds of trillions of liras and has reached the 720 trillion lira mark," said document.
It vowed to speed up the privatisation of the banking sector, complete the sale of Turk Telekom and increase revenues by widening the tax base and lowering some tax rates.
The constitutional court earlier this year approved the $3.5 billion privatisation of the telecommunications giant Turk Telekom.

Government officials say around four state banks are ready to be sold off if the political will were present. Another bank privatisation has been delayed by the agreed buyer's failure to make a downpayment.
